title: Preparing for Life as a Missionary
focus: Practice topic: making a personal preparation plan
intro: A mission asks for hard work with all one’s heart, might, mind and strength. In this lesson learners see how to start becoming a missionary now, in spirit, body and heart, and where to find help when it is hard.
preparation: Study 2 Nephi 4:19–26 and Alma 17:2–3, 9; 26:11–13; 29:10. Study Elder David A. Bednar, “Becoming a Missionary.” Prepare paper for each learner to write goals. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: Becoming a missionary now
paras: Ask: How do you expect your life to change when you begin your mission? What can you start doing now to prepare?

Read this from Elder David A. Bednar, “Becoming a Missionary,” general conference priesthood session, October 2005: you can begin “to think as missionaries think, to read what missionaries read, to pray as missionaries pray.” His counsel is for young women too. Ask how a person can become a missionary before the missionary training center.

Read Alma 17:2–3, 9 and Alma 17:11 about the sons of Mosiah. Ask what they did to prepare to teach with power and authority, and how learners can follow their example. Then give time to write goals, such as daily scripture study, morning and evening prayer, going to bed and rising on time, and less time on devices.

sections.title: Spiritual preparation
paras: Read Doctrine and Covenants 88:74. Ask what it means to be sanctified: to be clean and worthy of the Holy Ghost. Help learners see that the Lord asks His servants to be clean.

Read Elder M. Russell Ballard’s counsel on keeping our hearts, hands and minds clean, including staying away from pornography as we would a deadly disease. Show how Elder Jeffrey R. Holland pleaded with those on the Lord’s team to stay within the lines. Ask why failing to repent would limit a missionary.
Say clearly that anyone with a concern about worthiness should speak with his or her bishop, branch president or stake president now.

sections.title: Physical and emotional preparation
paras: A mission asks for a healthy body and a steady mind. Missionaries live a scheduled life: they are in bed by 10:30 in the evening and up by 6:30 in the morning. Ask learners to ponder how ready they are, and what they can do now about exercise, food and sleep.

Every missionary feels some stress, homesickness or doubt. President Gordon B. Hinckley felt discouraged after he arrived in the field and was lifted by going to work. Read Jeremiah 1:4–9, Alma 17:5, Alma 26:27 and Moses 6:31–32 to see that great servants of God felt weak too. Ask how it helps to know that every missionary faces challenges.

sections.title: Looking to the Lord for help
paras: Read 2 Nephi 4:17–19, then study 2 Nephi 4:19–26. Nephi felt sorrow over his weakness and then remembered the Lord’s goodness and trusted Him. Ask how remembering the Lord has helped learners in a hard time.

Read what Elder Jeffrey R. Holland taught about the Savior in Gethsemane and why missionaries can stand tall in struggle. Then read Alma 26:11–13, Alma 29:10 and Doctrine and Covenants 18:15–16. Explain that some needs also call for help from priesthood leaders and loved ones.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Show the three kinds of preparation
examples.text: Write three words on the board: spirit, body, heart. Ask learners to name one way to prepare in each, using Alma 17:2–3 and Doctrine and Covenants 88:74.

examples.title: Explain that every missionary has hard days
examples.text: Use Jeremiah 1:4–9, Alma 26:27 and Moses 6:31–32 to show that servants of God have felt weak and afraid. Say what helped them.

examples.title: Explain how Nephi found peace
examples.text: Read 2 Nephi 4:19–26 and write the steps Nephi took: remember, trust, pray, rejoice.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Make a goal in front of the class
examples.text: Choose one goal and write it using the Spirit’s help: what, when and how you will check. Say why you chose it.

examples.title: Share a hard day
examples.text: Tell a short story about when you felt weak and how you turned to the Lord. End with a testimony.

examples.title: Show how to ask for help
examples.text: Show how to talk with a priesthood leader or a trusted adult about a concern, in a few kind sentences.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Write goals and share
examples.text: Each learner writes three goals: one for spirit, one for body and one for heart. They share one with a partner.

examples.title: Teach 2 Nephi 4
examples.text: In pairs, teach a friend how Nephi overcame discouragement, using 2 Nephi 4:19–26 and one personal example.

examples.title: Practise the schedule
examples.text: Set a simple daily schedule for the week, with a sleep time, study time and prayer time. Share it with a partner.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand how to prepare for missionary life? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify that the Lord will magnify those who prepare and serve with all their heart. Invite learners to share one thing they will start this week.

tips.text: Work in small groups with a leader so every learner takes part.
Let learners write goals in a study journal while the Spirit is present.
Help learners apply principles in their own circumstances.
Invite returned missionaries to share how they handled stress.

quote.text: to think as missionaries think, to read what missionaries read, to pray as missionaries pray
quote.by: Elder David A. Bednar, “Becoming a Missionary,” general conference priesthood session, October 2005

study: Read 2 Nephi 4:19–26 together and ask what helped Nephi overcome his discouragement.
invitations: Think about what you need to do to be clean and worthy to serve. Speak with your bishop or branch president if needed.
Set personal goals for exercise, healthy food and sleep.
Ask a returned missionary how he or she handled stress and homesickness.

blocks.text: Welcome the class warmly. Begin with a prayer and a short thought from scripture to invite the Holy Ghost.
What happened when you tried last lesson’s invitation? Who would like to share?
Listen for: real experiences, effort made, one thing learned.
Try saying: “Before we start, who would like to tell us what happened when they tried last week’s invitation?”
Keep the review short. Let two or three learners share, and thank each one.
